title: The Discerning Upper Crust Would Approve

contact_edits.before: The two girls match them, with Sara Topham's impregnable hauteur as Gwendolen balanced by Andrea Runge's demurer steeliness as Cecily. As Reverend Chasuble, Stephen Ouimette, a visual symphony of limbs and gaiters, wafts phantasmally through the manor-house garden; Sarah Dodd's Miss Prism melts delightfully though always respectably in his presence. I thought at first she overdid her suburban asperity towards Cecily, on whom she is after all dependent, but on reflection she makes an excellent point. Prism, though personally as blinkered as Lady Bracknell, is the play's social conscience, prevented as a governess from aping the aristocracy as the butlers and valets do. And she has her unwitting revenge. One wouldn't want to throw the baby out with the bath-water, but leaving it in a handbag is an outrage as revolutionary as Aunt Augusta knew in her threatened bones that it would be. - The Importance of Being Earnest is in repertory through Oct. 30. 1-800-567-1600.
